meaning.en: A person with no selfish desires cannot be swayed or bought, and so stands upright and unyielding.
meaning.zh: 人没有私欲，就不会被利益左右，因而能刚正不阿。

equivalents: he who wants nothing fears nothing

examples.zh: 无欲则刚，他从不收礼，因此敢于直言。
examples.en: With no desire to gain, he never took gifts and so dared speak frankly.

examples.zh: 无欲则刚，对金钱看得淡的人，不怕被人要挟。
examples.en: Without craving, one is strong; those who care little for money cannot be blackmailed.

examples.zh: 她常把无欲则刚挂在嘴边，提醒自己不要贪心。
examples.en: She often cites 'no desire, no weakness' to remind herself not to be greedy.

story.en: Lin Zexu's study couplet reads: 'The sea takes in a hundred rivers, for its capacity is great; cliffs stand a thousand fathoms, for they have no desire' (海纳百川，有容乃大；壁立千仞，无欲则刚).
story.zh: 林则徐《题书房联》：“海纳百川，有容乃大；壁立千仞，无欲则刚。”

usage.en: Often quoted of officials and in self-cultivation; famously the second half of Lin Zexu's couplet 海纳百川，有容乃大；壁立千仞，无欲则刚.
usage.zh: 常用于称赞官员或自我修养；出自林则徐自勉联“海纳百川，有容乃大；壁立千仞，无欲则刚”。

literal: modest · respectful · lower oneself to · scholars

meaning.en: To treat talented people with humility and respect, despite one's high status.
meaning.zh: 地位高的人对有才能的人谦虚有礼、屈己待人。

examples.zh: 他身居高位却谦恭下士，因此贤才云集。
examples.en: Though high in rank, he treated able people with respect, so talent gathered around him.

examples.zh: 古代明君多谦恭下士，广纳人才。
examples.en: Wise rulers of old were modest toward scholars and welcomed talent.

examples.zh: 这位老教授谦恭下士，常向年轻人请教。
examples.en: The old professor is modest and often asks young people for advice.

usage.en: Predicate; literary, used of leaders and the powerful. 士 means scholars and able people.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语，用于位高权重者。“士”指读书人、有才之人。

meaning.en: Whoever wins gets to set the rules and the story; the victor takes all.
meaning.zh: 谁赢了谁就是王，成功的一方掌握话语权和一切。

equivalents: to the victor go the spoils

examples.zh: 商场上胜者为王，没人在乎你过程多辛苦。
examples.en: In business the winner takes all, and nobody cares how hard you worked.

examples.zh: 胜者为王，败者寇，历史往往由赢家书写。
examples.en: The winner is king, the loser a bandit; history is usually written by the victors.

examples.zh: 他信奉胜者为王，什么手段都敢用。
examples.en: He believes the winner takes all and will use any means.

usage.en: Often said cynically; the full pair is 胜者为王，败者为寇. Neutral as a statement, but often implies that ends justify means.
usage.zh: 常带有无奈或犬儒意味，全句为“胜者为王，败者为寇”。

pinyin: yī rén zhī xià, wàn rén zhī shàng
literal: one · person · 's · below, ten thousand · people · 's · above
natural: below one man, above ten thousand

meaning.en: Second only to the ruler in rank; holding the highest position of power below the top.
meaning.zh: 地位只在一个人（君主）之下，却在所有人之上，指权位极高。

examples.zh: 宰相是一人之下，万人之上的官职。
examples.en: The chancellor held a post below one man and above ten thousand.

examples.zh: 他一人之下，万人之上，公司大小事都由他定。
examples.en: Second only to the chairman, he decides everything in the company.

examples.zh: 副总理一人之下，万人之上，但责任也重。
examples.en: The deputy premier ranks just below the premier and above everyone else, but the burden is heavy.

usage.en: Originally of prime ministers; today used jokingly for number-two figures in companies or teams.
usage.zh: 本指宰相，今多用于调侃公司或团体里的二号人物。

pinyin: wèi tā rén zuò jià yī shang
literal: for · other · people · make · wedding · clothes
natural: to sew wedding dresses for others

meaning.en: To work hard only for others' benefit while getting no reward oneself.
meaning.zh: 辛苦做出的成果全给别人享用，自己一无所得。

equivalents: pull someone else's chestnuts out of the fire

examples.zh: 他熬夜写的方案被领导署名发表，真是为他人作嫁衣裳。
examples.en: His late-night proposal was published under his boss's name; he was just sewing wedding dresses for others.

examples.zh: 做代工的小厂，常常是为他人作嫁衣裳。
examples.en: Small contract manufacturers often work only for others' gain.

examples.zh: 辛苦培养的人才被挖走，不免觉得为他人作嫁衣裳。
examples.en: When the talent he trained was poached, he felt he'd done it all for others.

story.en: In Qin Taoyu's poem 'The Poor Girl', she resents that year after year she stitches gold thread 'only to make wedding clothes for others' (苦恨年年压金线，为他人作嫁衣裳).
story.zh: 秦韬玉《贫女》：“苦恨年年压金线，为他人作嫁衣裳。”

usage.en: Usually said with resentment or self-pity; the original poem is about a poor girl who weaves for brides.
usage.zh: 多含怨叹或自嘲之意；原诗写贫家女子替别人织嫁衣的辛酸。

pinyin: shì kě shā bù kě rǔ
literal: scholar · may · be killed · not · may · be humiliated
natural: a gentleman may be killed but not insulted

meaning.en: A person of principle would rather die than be humiliated.
meaning.zh: 有气节的人宁可被杀，也不能受侮辱。

equivalents: a man of honour will not be humiliated

examples.zh: 士可杀不可辱，他宁死也不肯低头认错。
examples.en: He would rather die than be humiliated, and refused to bow and admit fault.

examples.zh: 士可杀不可辱，你这样当众羞辱人，太过分了！
examples.en: A man of honour won't be insulted; humiliating people in public is too much!

examples.zh: 面对敌人的羞辱，他喊出“士可杀不可辱”。
examples.en: Facing the enemy's humiliation, he shouted that a gentleman can be killed but not insulted.

story.en: The Book of Rites says of the Confucian gentleman: 'He may be killed but not humiliated' (可杀而不可辱也).
story.zh: 《礼记·儒行》：“儒有可亲而不可劫也，可近而不可迫也，可杀而不可辱也。”

usage.en: Declarative; stresses dignity. Today also used in a half-joking way for small slights.
usage.zh: 多作表态之语，强调尊严；今天也常半开玩笑地用于小事。

meaning.en: Smooth, flattering talk undermines morality and judgment.
meaning.zh: 花言巧语会败坏道德、扰乱人的判断。

examples.zh: 巧言乱德，不要被甜言蜜语迷惑。
examples.en: Glib talk corrupts virtue; don't be taken in by sweet words.

examples.zh: 孔子说巧言乱德，提醒人们提防谄媚。
examples.en: Confucius said that clever words ruin virtue, warning people against flatterers.

examples.zh: 巧言乱德，会说话不等于有品德。
examples.en: Glib words confuse virtue; being a good talker is not being a good person.

story.en: Confucius said: 'Clever words confound virtue; lack of patience in small matters confounds great plans' (巧言乱德。小不忍，则乱大谋).
story.zh: 《论语·卫灵公》：“巧言乱德。小不忍，则乱大谋。”

usage.en: The Analects line continues 小不忍，则乱大谋. Quoted as a warning about flatterers and sophists.
usage.zh: 《论语》原文接“小不忍，则乱大谋”。用于警告人们提防谄媚和诡辩。

natural: the music of Zheng and Wei

meaning.en: The popular music of the states of Zheng and Wei, which Confucian moralists condemned as decadent; hence any music or entertainment regarded as frivolous or corrupting.
meaning.zh: 春秋时郑国、卫国的民间音乐，被儒家视为淫靡之音，后泛指被认为靡靡不正的音乐。

examples.zh: 在古代儒家眼里，流行小调不过是郑卫之音。
examples.en: In the eyes of ancient Confucians, popular tunes were just the music of Zheng and Wei.

examples.zh: 老先生斥责这首歌是郑卫之音，年轻人却觉得好听。
examples.en: The old gentleman condemned the song as decadent; young people thought it sounded fine.

examples.zh: 所谓郑卫之音，其实多是各地民歌。
examples.en: What is called Zheng-Wei music was mostly local folk songs.

story.en: The Book of Rites says: 'The music of Zheng and Wei is the music of a disordered age' (郑卫之音，乱世之音也).
story.zh: 《礼记·乐记》：“郑卫之音，乱世之音也，比于慢矣。”

usage.en: A moralistic label from the Confucian tradition; today used critically or to describe how tastes were judged in the past.
usage.zh: 带有儒家道德评判色彩，今多用于批评或说明古代对音乐的看法。

meaning.en: To aim for a project that is too large and too comprehensive, regardless of what is practical.
meaning.zh: 追求规模大、内容全，不顾实际条件。

equivalents: bite off more than one can chew

examples.zh: 这个方案贪大求全，结果什么都没做好。
examples.en: The plan was overambitious and in the end nothing was done well.

examples.zh: 创业初期不宜贪大求全，要先做好一个产品。
examples.en: In the early stage of a startup, don't overreach; do one product well first.

examples.zh: 他贪大求全，把展览办成了大杂烩。
examples.en: He went too big and too complete, turning the exhibition into a jumble.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; criticism of overreach in planning.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，批评规划脱离实际。

pinyin: bù jī kuǐ bù, wú yǐ zhì qiān lǐ
variants: 不积跬步，无以至千里；不积小流，无以成江海
literal: not · accumulate · half-steps, no · means · reach · thousand · li
natural: pile up small steps to reach a thousand li

meaning.en: Great distances are covered by accumulating small steps; big achievements come from steady daily effort.
meaning.zh: 一小步一小步地积累，就能走到千里之外，比喻大的成就要靠一点一滴的努力。

equivalents: a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step

examples.zh: 积跬步以至千里，学习没有捷径。
examples.en: Small steps add up to a thousand li; there is no shortcut in learning.

examples.zh: 她每天坚持写作，积跬步以至千里。
examples.en: She writes every day, covering a thousand li step by step.

examples.zh: 积跬步以至千里，再远的目标也能实现。
examples.en: Small steps add up; even a distant goal can be reached.

story.en: Xunzi: 'Without accumulating half-steps, you cannot reach a thousand li; without gathering small streams, you cannot make a river or sea' (不积跬步，无以至千里；不积小流，无以成江海).
story.zh: 《荀子·劝学》：“不积跬步，无以至千里；不积小流，无以成江海。”

usage.en: The original Xunzi wording is the negative 不积跬步，无以至千里 (without accumulating small steps, you cannot reach a thousand li). 跬 is a half-step.
usage.zh: 《荀子》原文是反面说法“不积跬步，无以至千里”。“跬”指半步。

natural: a chicken talking to a duck

meaning.en: A conversation in which neither side understands the other.
meaning.zh: 双方说话各说各的，彼此听不懂，无法沟通。

equivalents: like talking to a brick wall

examples.zh: 他讲粤语，我讲普通话，简直鸡同鸭讲。
examples.en: He spoke Cantonese and I spoke Putonghua; it was like a chicken talking to a duck.

examples.zh: 跟三岁小孩讲大道理，不过是鸡同鸭讲。
examples.en: Lecturing a three-year-old is just talking at cross purposes.

examples.zh: 两个部门各说各的，会议开成了鸡同鸭讲。
examples.en: The two departments each said their own piece, and the meeting became a dialogue of the deaf.

usage.en: Predicate or complement; originally a Cantonese saying (鸡同鸭讲, 'gāi tung ngaap góng') that has spread across Mandarin. It usually describes a failure to communicate rather than rudeness.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、补语，原为粤语俗语，后传入普通话。强调沟通不了，而非态度恶劣。

meaning.en: To lose one's early brilliance and end up no different from ordinary people.
meaning.zh: 原来才华出众，后来变得和普通人一样，毫无特别。

examples.zh: 神童长大后若不努力学习，也会泯然众人。
examples.en: A child prodigy who stops studying will end up like everybody else.

examples.zh: 他年少成名，后来却泯然众人。
examples.en: He found fame young, but later faded into the crowd.

examples.zh: 不要让天赋泯然众人，要靠后天努力。
examples.en: Don't let your gift fade into ordinariness; build on it with effort.

story.en: Wang Anshi tells of the child prodigy Fang Zhongyong, whose talent was wasted because he was never taught, so that 'he became one of the crowd' (泯然众人矣).
story.zh: 王安石《伤仲永》：“不使学，……卒之为众人，……泯然众人矣。”

usage.en: Predicate; cautionary. Often quoted from Wang Anshi's essay on Fang Zhongyong, a prodigy who wasted his talent.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于警示。常引自王安石《伤仲永》，讲神童方仲永因不学而沦为常人。

natural: if the heart is sincere, it works

meaning.en: If you are sincere enough, your prayer or wish will be answered; sincerity is what counts.
meaning.zh: 只要心意真诚，祈求或愿望就会灵验。

equivalents: where there's a will, there's a way

examples.zh: 拜佛不在乎香火多少，心诚则灵。
examples.en: In worshipping the Buddha, what matters is not the amount of incense but sincerity.

examples.zh: 心诚则灵，考前好好复习比求神更管用。
examples.en: Sincerity works, but careful revision before the exam helps more than praying.

examples.zh: 奶奶常说心诚则灵，每次出门都要祈福。
examples.en: Grandma always says sincerity makes prayers work, and prays for blessings whenever anyone sets out.

usage.en: Often said in religious settings; also used lightly, with or without belief, to mean that sincere effort matters. The saying often goes with 信则灵，不信则不灵.
usage.zh: 多用于宗教场合，也常半开玩笑地说诚意最重要。常与“信则灵，不信则不灵”并说。
